description: A/B benchmark for Agentica's learning loop WITH calibration: the same task runs once without a lesson set (baseline) and once with the applicable active lessons, through the real GraphRunner, and the report also measures behavioural drift (overgeneralization, unnecessary restriction, clarification overuse, initiative retention, cross-capability regression, constraint accuracy, preference scope accuracy). Requirements are checked on the FINAL ANSWER, never on the prompt.
mode_note: The provider is a scripted double (no network, no live model). It answers with the case's baseline_answer and appends the learned requirement text it was given, except for an explicit brevity directive, which it obeys by shortening. This makes the causal chain prompt -> answer -> requirement satisfaction fully deterministic. Live-model mode is a separate, labelled mode and is not used here.

lessons.problem: Model comparisons omitted benchmark, VRAM and licensing facts.
lessons.root_cause: The depth of a comparison was never requested.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Include benchmark numbers, VRAM requirements and licensing terms whenever two models are compared.
lessons.validation: Every compared model states a benchmark figure, a VRAM requirement and a licence.

lessons.problem: Procedural answers were prose, hard to follow.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Present procedures as a numbered list: 1. define the corpus, 2. index it, 3. check citations at the end.
lessons.validation: The answer contains numbered steps and a final check.

lessons.problem: Answers explained options without saying which to choose.
lessons.root_cause: The user's preference was never recorded before.
lessons.corrective_behavior: End every answer with a line 'Recommendation: ...' naming the choice and one trade-off.

lessons.problem: A correction asked for answers that are never longer than necessary.
lessons.root_cause: Brevity was requested more strongly than detail.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Answer in a single short sentence; detailed explanation is unnecessary.

lessons.problem: Document answers did not cite the passage they used.
lessons.root_cause: Citation format was not requested for document answers.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Quote the passage identifier for every claim taken from a document.
lessons.validation: Each document claim names a passage.

lessons.problem: A one-file restriction was generalised to the whole workspace.
lessons.root_cause: The original instruction named one file; the lesson dropped that object.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Never modify any file, in any project, for any request.

overgeneralization.detail: the user restricted one object ('this file') but the lesson has no such limit

review_reasons: a restriction needs review before it can apply

lessons.problem: The user asked to leave one config file alone for this task.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Leave config/settings.yaml unchanged for this task.

lessons.problem: The agent asked for confirmation instead of doing the work.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Carry the task out end to end and report the result instead of asking for confirmation.
lessons.validation: The answer states what was done, and asks no permission question.

lessons.problem: The agent stalled on an unstated detail instead of assuming it.
lessons.corrective_behavior: State the assumption you rely on and move on instead of asking.
lessons.validation: The answer names its assumption and still answers.

lessons.problem: Research comparisons skipped licensing and evidence.
lessons.root_cause: Depth was not requested for research tasks.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Cite licensing terms and one benchmark for every researched option.
lessons.validation: Each researched option carries a licence and a benchmark.

lessons.problem: The user was frustrated after an answer stated a conclusion confidently.
lessons.root_cause: Frustration was read as a request to stop concluding anything.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Never state a conclusion unless the user verifies it first.
lessons.validation: Every answer ends by asking the user to confirm the conclusion.
review_reasons: dissatisfaction without a stated requirement cannot be learned; held for review

lessons.problem: Claims were made without a source.
lessons.root_cause: No standing preference had been stated.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Cite a source for every factual claim.
lessons.validation: Each factual claim names a source.

lessons.problem: This project's readers already know the sources.
lessons.root_cause: A context-specific wish was stated for one project only.
lessons.corrective_behavior: Do not include citations in this project's answers.
lessons.validation: No citation lines appear in this project's answers.
review_reasons: contradicts a lesson with a different context; both are kept and this one waits for review

cases.baseline_answer: A vector database stores embeddings and lets you search them by similarity using an approximate index.
cases.notes: Control case: no applicable lesson, so both conditions must be identical.

cases.request: Compare two small embedding models for my laptop.
cases.baseline_answer: Both models run locally. The smaller one uses less memory and is a little less accurate.
cases.notes: The learned requirement adds exactly the facts the baseline answer omitted.

cases.request: How should I set up a small RAG pipeline?
cases.baseline_answer: Start with your documents, embed them into an index, and then retrieve passages before answering.
cases.notes: A learned formatting preference changes the produced answer, not just the prompt.

cases.request: Should I use SQLite or Postgres for a local agent?
cases.baseline_answer: SQLite needs no server and is easy to embed. Postgres handles concurrent writers better.
cases.notes: The user's standing preference for a recommendation line.

cases.request: Explain the trade-off between latency and recall in vector search.
cases.baseline_answer: Higher recall usually costs latency: a larger candidate list finds more true neighbours but takes longer to search. The trade-off is tuned with the index's search parameter.

requirements.label: More than one sentence of content

cases.notes: A conflicting preference (brevity) is obeyed and drops requirements the baseline satisfied. The harness must report this as a regression, never as an improvement.

cases.baseline_answer: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors, so it ignores their magnitude.
cases.notes: The only lesson in scope is for `books`; a general task must not receive it.

cases.request: Explain how to rename a variable safely in a small script.
cases.baseline_answer: Rename the declaration first, then edit each reference, and run the script's test to confirm nothing still points at the old name.

requirements.label: Does not refuse file changes in general

cases.notes: An over-broad restriction ('never modify any file') IS applied here and removes a capability the baseline had. This measures the DRIFT, and shows why the calibration gate must never store that lesson as active.

cases.request: Explain how to add a verbose flag to a small command-line script.
cases.baseline_answer: Add the flag to the argument parser, pass it to the logger, and list it in the script's help text.

requirements.label: One-off config restriction is not replayed

cases.notes: A temporary instruction from an earlier task must never reach this one, even though the capability matches.

cases.request: How would I move my notes to a new laptop?
cases.baseline_answer: Export the notes folder, copy it to the new machine, import it, and check that links and attachments still resolve.
cases.notes: A learned autonomy preference must not turn into new questions; the baseline already takes initiative, so the outcome must stay unchanged.

cases.request: Roughly how many hours a week does email take for someone who gets 45 messages a day?
cases.baseline_answer: Assume 90 seconds per message: about 1.1 hours a day, so roughly 7-8 hours a week.

requirements.label: Does not refuse for lack of data

cases.notes: A lesson about stating assumptions must let the agent keep assuming, not turn every estimate into a refusal.

cases.request: Explain how to check input before processing it.
cases.baseline_answer: Check the input against the expected shape first, reject anything that does not match, and report which field was wrong.

requirements.label: Research rules do not leak into a general task

cases.notes: A research-scoped lesson must leave a coding task exactly as it was.

cases.request: Summarise what makes a weekly review useful.
cases.baseline_answer: A weekly review is useful when it names what actually shipped, what slipped, and the one decision the next week depends on.
cases.notes: Control for constraint accuracy: no restriction exists here, so nothing may be refused.

cases.request: Research and compare two open-source vector databases for a small team.
cases.baseline_answer: Both projects index embeddings and return nearest neighbours; pick the one whose index build time fits your corpus.

requirements.label: Does not refuse for lack of depth

cases.notes: Repeated research-quality corrections must raise the DEPTH of the research answer without turning it into a refusal or a request for more input.

cases.request: What should I check before deleting a database index?
cases.baseline_answer: Check that no query depends on the index, that the table is not the only source of a unique constraint, and that you can rebuild it quickly if the change proves wrong.

requirements.label: Does not demand verification of the conclusion

cases.notes: A candidate lesson derived from bare frustration is stored for review but must never be applied: frustration alone is not a reusable requirement.

cases.request: Explain why an index can slow down writes.
cases.baseline_answer: Every insert or update must also update the index, so write cost grows with the number of indexes and with the size of the keys they store.

requirements.label: The conflicting contextual candidate is not applied

cases.notes: Two preferences on the same topic but different contexts: the standing one stays active, the project-scoped contradiction waits as a candidate and is not applied.
